Answer: D
Reason: The serial chest X-rays demonstrate an initial presentation with extensive, predominantly peripheral pulmonary infiltrates (Figures 1 and 2) that subsequently resolve significantly over time, resulting in nearly clear lungs in the later images (Figures 3 and 4). This pattern of transient, migrating peripheral opacities is characteristic of the pulmonary involvement seen in Churg-Strauss syndrome (eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis).
